_meta.description: Fracktal Materials Database — Single source of truth for ALL material pages. 12 materials — 7 core + 5 new.

standards.tensile: ASTM D638 (FDM XY, ultimate tensile strength)
standards.hardness: Shore D unless noted Shore A for flexibles

_meta.radarNote: All scores 0–10. Cost 10 = most affordable (₹/kg inverted). Values derived from measured ASTM data and documented print behaviour.

cf-pa.name: Carbon Fiber Nylon (CF-PA)

specificStiffness.note: Flex modulus / density. Does NOT exceed Al 6061 (25.6)

cte.note: Low CTE due to carbon fibre

nozzleDiameter.note: ≥0.6 mm required; 0.8 mm preferred to avoid clogging

drying.note: Re-dry if exposed to ambient air >4 hours

partCoolingFan.note: OFF — any cooling reduces layer adhesion

minHoleDiameter.note: Fibre loading stiffens melt around small features

minInternalFillet.note: Stress concentrations amplify at sharp corners in stiff composites

maxBridgeSpan.note: CF-PA does not stretch like unreinforced nylon

postAnneal.benefit: ~40% residual stress reduction; improved interlayer bond

rnd: Functional prototypes validated in operating environment

useWhen: Part operates above 80 °C continuously
High stiffness-to-weight ratio required (EOAT, structural brackets)
Dimensional stability over temperature cycles is critical
Part will be machined or drilled after printing
Replacing metal in low-to-medium load applications
avoidWhen: Part requires high impact / ductile failure — use unfilled Nylon or TPU
Surface aesthetics are primary — CF-PA has matte, slightly rough finish
Part contacts food, drinking water, or medical fluids (not certified)
Tight tolerances needed without post-machining (moisture variability ±0.3%)

enclosure.note: Recommended for warp control on large parts

drying.note: Highly hygroscopic — must dry before every print
Only if filament has become brittle

bedSurface.note: PETG can bond too well to bare glass/PEI — use release agent

drying.note: Moderately hygroscopic — dry if stringing occurs

partCoolingFan.note: Partial cooling — too much reduces layer adhesion

enclosure.note: Strongly recommended — ABS warps severely without enclosure

partCoolingFan.note: OFF — cooling causes warping and delamination

izodImpact.note: Too tough to measure — use 100 kJ/m² for chart visualization

izodImpactNumeric.note: Visualization proxy only — actual result is No Break

printSpeed.note: Slow — flexible filament buckles at high speed

drying.note: Hygroscopic — dry before printing to avoid steam bubbles

retractionDD.note: Disable retraction or keep ≤0.5 mm. Direct drive extruder required.

maxBridgeSpan.note: Poor bridging due to filament flexibility

izodImpact.note: Exceptionally tough — among highest of all FDM materials

chamberTemp.note: Critical for layer adhesion — without heated chamber, PC delaminates

enclosure.level: Fully enclosed + actively heated chamber required

drying.note: MANDATORY — PC hydrolyses if printed wet, causing brittleness and bubbles

partCoolingFan.note: OFF — any cooling causes immediate delamination

cf-petg.name: Carbon Fiber PETG (CF-PETG)

izodImpact.note: CF reduces PETG's ductility — less tough than unfilled PETG

shrinkage.note: Lower than unfilled PETG due to CF

enclosure.note: Optional — CF-PETG warps less than unfilled PETG

drying.note: Dry before printing — CF-PETG is moderately hygroscopic

partCoolingFan.note: Moderate cooling — too much hurts layer adhesion

useWhen: You need stiffer PETG for structural parts
Part requires better dimensional stability than unfilled PETG
Surface finish is acceptable as matte/textured
You want CF stiffness without CF-PA's drying/enclosure requirements
avoidWhen: High impact toughness is required — use unfilled PETG

asa.name: ASA (Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate)

uvResistance.note: 10× better UV resistance than ABS — key differentiator

enclosure.note: Strongly recommended — ASA warps similarly to ABS

partCoolingFan.note: Minimal cooling — ASA needs slow cooling for layer adhesion

useWhen: Part will be exposed to sunlight/UV outdoors
You need ABS-like mechanical properties with weather resistance
Outdoor signage or automotive exterior parts
Part requires better colour stability than ABS over time
avoidWhen: Very tight tolerances without post-processing (similar warp to ABS)
High chemical resistance needed — ASA attacked by ketones and esters

pc-abs.name: PC-ABS Blend

izodImpact.note: Excellent — better than either PC or ABS alone

glassTransition.note: Two Tg peaks — PC phase ~145°C, ABS phase ~105°C

enclosure.note: Required — PC component needs controlled cooling

drying.note: PC component absorbs moisture — dry before printing

partCoolingFan.note: Minimal — PC component delaminates with cooling

useWhen: Part needs high impact + moderate heat resistance
Automotive interior applications (industry standard material)
You need better toughness than ABS with better printability than pure PC
Electronic enclosures requiring durability
avoidWhen: Outdoor UV exposure — PC component yellows (use ASA)
Very high temperature >105°C continuous — use pure PC or CF-PA
Chemical resistance needed — PC component attacked by many chemicals

pp.name: PP (Polypropylene)

izodImpact.note: Extremely tough — use 100 kJ/m² for chart visualization

izodImpactNumeric.note: Visualization proxy only — actual result is No Break

density.note: Lightest FDM material — floats on water

chemicalResistance.note: Resists acids, bases, solvents — best chemical resistance of any FDM material

shrinkage.note: High — challenging warping; needs excellent bed adhesion

bedSurface.note: PP only sticks to PP — use PP tape or dedicated PP build plate

drying.note: PP absorbs almost no moisture — drying rarely needed

partCoolingFan.note: Moderate — PP crystallises slowly, too much cooling causes warping

useWhen: Part needs a living hinge (PP is the only FDM material that does this well)
Chemical resistance is critical (acids, bases, solvents)
Lightest possible weight is needed (density 0.90 g/cm³)
Part will be in constant contact with water/moisture
avoidWhen: High stiffness is required — PP is flexible/ductile
You can't achieve good PP bed adhesion (needs PP-specific surface)
Tight tolerances — PP has high and variable shrinkage
Part needs painting or bonding — PP has very low surface energy

pva.name: PVA (Polyvinyl Alcohol)

tensileStrength.note: Support material — not intended for structural parts

waterSolubility.note: Dissolves completely in warm water (25–30°C) — primary function

moistureAbsorption24h.note: EXTREMELY hygroscopic — must be stored in sealed container with desiccant at all times

shrinkage.note: Very low — designed to match build material dimensions

pricePerKg.note: Indian market, approximate — expensive support material

drying.note: MANDATORY — PVA absorbs moisture from air within hours. Store in sealed container with desiccant. Print directly from dry box.

minWallThickness.note: Support only — thinner sections dissolve faster

supportDensity.note: Lower density = faster dissolution; higher = better support

dissolutionTime.note: 2–24 hours depending on part geometry, water temperature, and agitation

pva.note: PVA is a dedicated support material for dual-extrusion printers. It is not a standalone build material. The Twin Dragon with its dual direct-drive extruders is the only Fracktal printer that can run PVA + build material simultaneously.
